title: 60s receiveTypingIndicators cache TTL hardcoded
description:
File: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md
Lines: 398-400

Current text:
  "Servers that cache a remote participant's `receiveTypingIndicators` value SHOULD use a TTL of no more than 60 seconds, as there is no federation notification mechanism when a remote user updates this preference."

The cache exists only inside the sending server's memory. Nothing about its TTL is observable on the wire. The only externally observable behavior is "how stale a remote preference may be when we suppress vs. forward typing". Different deployments have legitimately different tolerance:
- A high-trust bilateral federation between corporate peers may tolerate hours
- An open federation between strangers may want seconds

60 seconds is a deployment-internal parameter masquerading as a normative requirement.

Suggested rewording:
  "Servers that cache a remote participant's `receiveTypingIndicators` value SHOULD use a short TTL; the specific value is implementation-defined. As there is no federation notification mechanism when a remote user updates this preference, the TTL chosen affects how long a stale value may persist after a remote user opts out of typing-indicator forwarding."
acceptance_criteria:
- The 60-second number is removed
- The guidance about lack-of-federation-notification consequence is retained
- No companion change required in the main draft (the field itself is appropriately spec'd at line 451)
